mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of 2% or more signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and compresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves positive 60-day returns in more than 70% of triggered episodes despite the consumption decline.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) that falls below 3.5% for two consecutive months indicates an extremely tight labor market, which raises wage inflation and input costs, ultimately pressuring profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of such episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate earnings and capital spending, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL (CPI) above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual shock of monetary tightening and accelerating inflation, which increases real discount rates and erodes real earnings, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both above 12-month moving average
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of such dual-triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated monthly decline in both real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) and retail sales (RSAFS) of at least 0.3% signals deteriorating consumer purchasing power and demand pressure, which reduces corporate top-line growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and RSAFS both fall > -0.3% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 60-day returns in more than 55% of such dual-triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 6% for two consecutive months, combined with a concurrent decline in industrial production (INDPRO) of more than 0.5%, signals a deepening recessionary environment, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 6% for 2 consecutive months AND INDPRO falls > -0.5% in the same months
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of such dual-triggered recession episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the Housing Starts Index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals a recovery in residential construction demand, which boosts materials, finance, and retail sectors and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12-month moving average for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of triggered housing recovery episodes.
